s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive pigmented skin lesion with irregular borders and variable coloration, presenting with satellite lesions and areas of regression
salient_findings: Irregular brown-black patch on the left lateral ankle
Satellite lesions surrounding the primary patch
Areas of regression within the patch
key_facts: Age of initial presentation: 6 years
Location of the lesion: left lateral ankle
Size of the lesion at age 6: 3.6 × 3 cm
Size of the lesion at age 9: 5.5 × 5 cm
Presence of satellite lesions
Asymptomatic nature of the lesion
Dermoscopy findings: discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas
Histopathology findings: atypical compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction
Gene Expression Testing score: -7.1
Presence of areas of regression within the patch

shortlist.label: Atypical Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology findings of atypical compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction

shortlist.label: Congenital Melanocytic Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large, dark brown patch with satellite lesions and areas of regression, consistent with a congenital melanocytic nevus

shortlist.label: Dysplastic Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Dermoscopy findings of discontiguous and irregular homogenous blue, brown, and gray areas, and histopathology findings of atypical nevus

shortlist.label: Melanoma
shortlist.why_kept: Although the gene expression testing score is consistent with a benign nevus, the presence of atypical features and areas of regression warrant consideration of melanoma

shortlist.label: Pigmented Spindle Cell Nevus
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology findings of atypical nevus with random nuclear atypia and broad areas of regressive fibrosis, which can be seen in pigmented spindle cell nevus

raw.rationale: The histopathology findings of a compound nevus with large nested melanocytes and bridging at the dermal-epidermal junction, along with the gene expression testing score of -7.1, which is consistent with a benign nevus, support the diagnosis of an atypical nevus. The presence of areas of regression within the patch also aligns with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Congenital Melanocytic Nevus
rejected.why: The lesion first appeared at age 6, which is not typical for congenital melanocytic nevi that are usually present at birth.

rejected.label: Dysplastic Nevus
rejected.why: While dysplastic nevi can exhibit atypical features, the specific histopathological and dermoscopic findings in this case more closely align with an atypical nevus.

rejected.label: Melanoma
rejected.why: The gene expression testing score and the absence of other high-risk features for melanoma make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Pigmented Spindle Cell Nevus
rejected.why: The histopathological description does not specifically mention spindle cells, which are characteristic of pigmented spindle cell nevi.
